title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 35-38): Grothendieck is axiomatising 'ateliers'. An atelier is a structure (𝓕, ≤, ≪): a set of 'figures' ordered by inclusion ≤, with a second, stronger relation ≪ (plausibly 'F is relatively compact / well inside G'), subject to axioms At1-At7. 𝓜 ⊂ 𝓕 is the set of elementary figures ('multistructures'), the sup-irreducible elements, and every figure is recovered from the elementary figures below it. Fig(L) is the atelier of all figures of a 'lieu' L. An atelier is 'ensembliste' if p: 𝓕 → Fig(L) identifies it with a sub-atelier of Fig(L).

This page continues the definition of a morphism f: 𝓕 → 𝓕' begun on p. 36. The conditions are:
(a) f is increasing for both ≤ and ≪.
(b) For every down-set F ⊂ 𝓜 that comes from a figure (the set of elementary figures below it), the saturated image f_sat(F) again comes from a figure.
So a morphism is essentially determined by a map on irreducibles that preserves representable down-sets. This is a Birkhoff/Stone-type passage between a lattice and its poset of join-irreducibles.

NB claims:
- f has a property P iff f_sat has it.
- f is an isomorphism onto a sub-atelier iff f is an order-embedding for ≤ and ≪ and its image is 'F-closed'.

Grothendieck then tries to define a sub-atelier 𝓕' ⊂ 𝓕: with the induced ≤ and ≪ it should be an atelier, and the inclusion should be a morphism. Concretely:
1° 𝓕' is stable under the Sups, computed in 𝓕, of suitable families (bounded above?) of its members.
2° The same holds for infs (∩F_i).
He asks whether it would be more reasonable to impose instead:
(B) 𝓕' is downward closed, i.e. every sub-figure of a member of 𝓕' lies in 𝓕'.
He notes that one must check that (B) suffices to make 𝓕' an atelier. 'Strict' sub-ateliers correspond to down-closed subsets 𝓜' ⊂ 𝓜.

The margin objects that sub-ateliers arising as images f(𝓜) ⊂ 𝓜' need not be strict. One should also require F ∨ F' ∈ 𝓕' whenever the join exists. The aim is that an ensembliste atelier realises 𝓜 as a set of elementary figures in L.

The next page settles the definition: a sub-atelier is a non-empty down-closed subset stable under the non-empty Sups existing in 𝓕'. It is 'spécieux' if stable under arbitrary existing Sups. One then checks that 𝓜' = 𝓕' ∩ 𝓜 is exactly the set of irreducibles of 𝓕'.

Purpose: building the categorical/order-theoretic foundations (morphisms, subobjects) of a combinatorial 'analysis situs', i.e. the tame topology announced in Esquisse d'un programme.
errors: The page is exploratory and the definitions are not stabilised. Condition (B) (down-closure) alone does not give stability under existing Sups, so it does not replace 1°. Grothendieck's own margin and p. 38 correct this by requiring down-closure plus stability under non-empty Sups.
The NB characterisation (iso onto sub-atelier ⇔ embedding for ≤ and ≪ with F-closed image) is stated without proof. 'F-closed' is not defined on this page.
Condition 2° (stability under ∩/inf) is abandoned on the next page. As written, it conflicts with merely down-closed sub-ateliers when the infs are computed in 𝓕 versus 𝓕'.

ideas.what: Morphism of ateliers: a map monotone for ≤ and ≪ that sends representable down-sets of irreducibles to representable ones (via f_sat).
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of posets with auxiliary relation; Birkhoff/Priestley-type duality between lattices and posets of join-irreducibles

ideas.what: Sub-atelier as a down-closed subset stable under existing joins; correspondence of strict sub-ateliers with down-sets 𝓜' of elementary figures.
ideas.modern_name: Down-sets / ideals closed under existing joins; sublocales/subspaces via join-irreducibles

ideas.what: Axiomatising a 'space of figures' by an order ≤ together with a second relation ≪ (well-inside).
ideas.modern_name: de Vries compingent algebras; continuous lattices with way-below; (strong) proximity lattices
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'ateliers' (inclusion ≤ plus strong relation ≪, figures generated by sup-irreducible elementary figures) closely parallel structures from domain theory and point-free topology: de Vries algebras, proximity lattices, continuous lattices. Those structures axiomatise compact/stably compact spaces by a lattice with a 'well-inside' relation. No literature links his 1986 analysis-situs ateliers to these.
missed.quote: f soit croissante pour ≤ et ≪ ... munie des relations d'ordre ≤_𝓕', ≪_𝓕 induites
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Reading ateliers as proximity-lattice-like objects could make Grothendieck's tame-topology foundations comparable with o-minimal and point-free approaches. It could also tell us whether his axioms At1-At7 define a known duality.

missed.claim: The theory of morphisms and sub-ateliers (the iso-onto-sub-atelier criterion, the role of f_sat, ensembliste realisation in Fig(L)) is left as a sketch and never developed in published form.
missed.quote: Il faut vérifier que cette condition suffit à ce que (𝓕', ≤_𝓕', ≪_𝓕') soit bien un atelier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is part of the unexplored formal core of Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée'. Its interest is mainly historical unless the full axiom system is reconstructed.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational bookkeeping: morphisms and subobjects of an order-theoretic structure, with standard lattice-theoretic content. The only point of interest is that ateliers (≤ plus ≪) are an unpublished Grothendieck formalism resembling proximity lattices and de Vries algebras.
transcription_corrections: 'unipotents' (1°) is doubtful; the word looks more like 'majorés' or a similar condition on the family. The 'stabilité par Sup ...' parenthesis likely repeats the same qualifier.
'Sup_{i(𝓕)} F_i' should read Sup_i F_i computed in 𝓕, i.e. 'Sup_i^{(𝓕)}'.
In the NB the iso criterion reads roughly 'il faut et suffit que f soit un plongement pour ≤ et ≪, et que l'image soit F-fermée*', with an asterisk referring to the margin note.
'dans L' at the bottom is underlined in the image; the last line reads 'Ainsi, dans la définition de la page précédente, il faudrait donc ...'.
